statement: A school club has $12$ committees. Each committee has exactly $5$ members, and each club member serves on exactly $3$ committees. How many members does the club have?

choices.misconception: I divided the 12 committees by the 3 committees per member and never used the committee size.
I multiplied the 12 committees by the 3 committees per member, mixing up which count each number belongs to.
I counted the 12 x 5 = 60 committee seats as 60 different people, but each person fills 3 seats.
I multiplied all three numbers 12 x 5 x 3, as if each seat on a committee came with three more people.

hints: Count the seats on committees in two different ways.
Each pair (member, committee the member is on) is counted once from the committee side and once from the member side. Set the two counts equal.
From committees: $12 \cdot 5 = 60$ seats. From members: $3$ seats each. So $3m = 60$.

solutions.reliable: Count the pairs (person, committee) where the person sits on that committee. Each of the $12$ committees has $5$ members, so there are $12 \cdot 5 = 60$ such pairs. Each member is in exactly $3$ pairs, so if there are $m$ members then $3m = 60$ and $m = 20$. Transferable idea: double counting, count one set of pairs from both sides and set the counts equal.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
